d9_boundary.question: how is this distinct from the D-9-quarantined ct_deployment_overlay / reliability_deployment_overlay?
d9_boundary.answer: those overlays pin measured ENERGY (a realized outcome, rule-13 forbidden). F3 feeds the INSTRUCTION STATE at the physical LSL — an operator input of the outage-window class, which rule 13 names as its own admissible example family. It is never realized output and never a per-unit model crosswalk (class grain; item 11 / Q-B stays FINAL-closed).
d9_boundary.d9_result: PASS — every quarantined overlay reads False/None in the arm, as in the control.
d9_boundary.rule19_incumbents_reconciled: the gas commitment bridge (CC) and the ST_GAS net-load drag already floor the same fleet; F3 composes by MAXIMUM with tie-keeps-incumbent attribution, so it never stacks (rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH]).

mechanism_engaged.verdict: YES — the floor is live and attributable

G-SHORTFALL.rule: per rigid family, arm shortfall hour-set ⊆ control's (precommit AMENDMENT 1 — no MANUFACTURED shortage; the keeper baseline itself carries 21 designed VOLL-engagement hours)

window_check.reading: the WINDOW leg passes by construction, exactly as declared in D4_WINDOWS — the measured ONRUC series carries its own window, so there are no off-window hours to bind in.

verdict.disposition: REJECTED-AS-ARMED (G-D2 / D-4 unit-conduct FAIL), with zero benefit
verdict.gate_failure: G-D2 — 2 new D-4 rows for ercot_ruc_commitment; 23 of 42 unit-conduct rows FAIL, carrying 94% of the mechanism's floored energy (0.0082 of 0.0087 TWh) over 1,886 binding unit-hours on units whose measured CEMS generation is ZERO in the majority of those hours (measured_median_mw 0.0, measured_zero_share 0.55-1.00).
verdict.benefit: NONE. d_price_at_miss p50 = max = 0.0 and improved_miss_hours = 0 — the floor moves nothing at the 114 missed scarcity hours. Official scores print the keeper digits unchanged; the probe-basis C3a is 0.01 pp WORSE (-29.99 -> -30.00) and the model mean falls 38.81 -> 38.80.
verdict.measured_cause: THE GRAIN, not the driver. The measured ONRUC instruction identifies ~2,031 SPECIFIC unit-hours on ~70 SPECIFIC units. Barred from the per-unit crosswalk (item 11 / Q-B FINAL), the mechanism distributes the class MW PRO-RATA across every unit in the class — so it reproduces the class MW total while attributing it to units the measured record says were offline. That is rule 17 [R-FLOOR-WINDOW] by its own definition: a floor binding in hours its own driver evidence says the unit is not running is a bug, whatever it does to the residual. The class-grain form is the ONLY admissible grain here, and it provably mis-locates the instruction.
verdict.structural_reading: F3 is refuted at the level of REPRESENTABILITY, not of data. The 2023 RUC object is real and 6.7x larger than the ercot97 lane measured — but ERCOT's out-of-market commitment is an inherently PER-UNIT instruction, and this model cannot place it per-unit under the standing Q-B closure. Any future re-open must first reopen the grain question, not the data question.

do_not_redo: Do NOT re-test the class-grain pro-rata form — it is adjudicated by a solved D-4 unit-conduct failure with 94% of its energy mis-placed. The ONLY route back is a grain change (per-unit placement), which is separately closed by item 11 / Q-B FINAL and would need its own owner instrument.
field_disposition: ercot_ruc_commitment_floor stays BUILT, default-off, registered (rule 26 does not apply — measured-input mechanism, zero fitted scalars, adjudicated by probe). The derive and the 2023 series stay: they are the sizing record that overturned the ercot97 premise.
